chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar al-Yamānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If we say something concerning a man, and it is not in him but is in his son or the son of his son, then do not deny that, for Allah, Exalted is He, does whatever He wills.

key_terms.اللَّهَ تَعَالَى: Allah, Exalted is He; the One whose will governs all outcomes
key_terms.تُنْكِرُوا: deny or reject; the response the Imam عليه السلام forbids
key_terms.رَجُلٍ: a man; the individual about whom a statement is made
key_terms.قَوْلًا: a statement or pronouncement made regarding someone
key_terms.وَلَدِ وَلَدِهِ: the son of his son; indicating fulfillment in a grandson or later descendant
key_terms.وَلَدِهِ: his son; indicating fulfillment in direct offspring
key_terms.يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ: He does whatever He wills; expressing divine volition and authority

ai.seo_question: How can a statement about one person be fulfilled in his son or grandson according to a hadith from al-Kāfī?
ai.summary: The hadith teaches that a statement made regarding a person may be fulfilled not in him directly, but in his descendants. It instructs the listener not to reject such a matter, since Allah, Exalted is He, acts according to His will. The narration points to divine wisdom in the unfolding of matters across generations.
